title: Contact between black and white musicians
summary: He says contact was rare and risky, including a 1954 Dallas incident.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In the '20s, and even in the early '30swas there much contact between black and white musicians?

It was select and rare.Like, a white guy get a chance to play with some black musicians, he was happy as hell. Cop catch you around in a black neighborhood and beat the hell out of him. Make 'em get on away from there. Some white boys were more daring than others. Some white boys didn't give a damn. They'd take a whippin'.........Shit......... I remember
in Dallas when I was there, take '54...as late as '54, this white guy came up playing in a club. Cop beat the hell out of him.

There's some rare...some isolated cases. They find out that you're all right. For example, like they found out I was all right. Right there in Dallas fifty years worked at the Elks Club, you know, white club, so they would give me a break more so than they would some other guy that they didn't like. Because they had Jim Crow laws and they could enforce it if (inaudible) they wanted to. And many of them did. But as a whole, I think that I was fortunate, to get through all this and ..end up telling some of it on paper. Talking about it.
